Variants.Content: Sisterton () is the chief port town of the Three Sisters, nominally part of the Vale yet possessing a far stronger island character than the Vale's interior. Fog, reefs, smuggling, fishing, and the sea lanes of the Narrow Sea shape this place; mainland nobles often regard the islanders as rough or untrustworthy, while the islanders themselves care more about whether boats make it back to harbor and whether salt can be traded for grain. Sisterton links the sea lanes running toward the Vale, White Harbor, Braavos, and the Crownlands; specific rulers and trade terms may change, but the geographical significance of the island port does not.
Entry Sisterton Local families also rely on goats, thin fields, orchards, and pack teams crossing the Mingyue Mountains; if any road, well, or dock fails, the price falls first on them.

Entry Sisterton They also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the valley; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, but true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hoof.

Entry Sisterton If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

Sisterton is more than a lord's hall; ship-repair timber, sailcloth, salt, catches of fish, and stone that withstands the sea wind shape this place just as much as chapels of the Seven, the threat of the mountain clans, and Andal knightly tradition. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Sisterton They care about goats, thin fields, orchards, and pack teams crossing the Mingyue Mountains. They also look at whether seeds are left after collecting grain, and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
